replies.What is your relationship with mathemati: Honestly, maths has always been a source of stress for me. It's not that I hate it, but it feels so abstract and disconnected from my interests like art and history. I find myself dreading math classes and often struggle to see the point in it all.
replies.Do you ever get anxious when thinking ab: Yes, absolutely! The thought of numbers and formulas makes me feel overwhelmed and anxious. My high neuroticism score probably contributes to this, making even simple calculations feel daunting and triggering a sense of panic before I even begin.
replies.Did you ever use AI to support your math: Not really, mostly because I avoid maths when I can. But if I did try using it, I think I'd find it intimidating at first since I'm not confident in my own abilities. However, having a patient tutor might help ease that anxiety slightly.
replies.How would you explain, step by step, how: I actually don't know this well because I've avoided maths topics like this for so long. If someone taught me gently and patiently, I could probably learn it over time, but right now, explaining it feels very difficult and stressful.

I'm not comfortable explaining this yet. Stationary points involve calculus concepts like derivatives that I've always found challenging and confusing. I'd need a lot of time and support from someone who understands my anxiety to really grasp these ideas.
replies.Briefly, how do you perform a Principal: PCA is definitely one of those topics that scares me because it's so complex. I would probably feel very anxious trying to explain it without proper guidance. It might help if someone broke it down slowly and made it less intimidating.
replies.According to you, how can LLMs be used t: LLMs could be amazing for students like me who get anxious around maths! They can provide instant, patient support and explain concepts gently without judgment. Having a friendly AI tutor might help reduce the fear and make learning feel more manageable.
